findings.finding: Undo can destroy another person's work. UNDO_GRACE_MS=2000 ignores real edits within 2 seconds and compares browser Date.now with server stamps. New-item undos lack kind and skip conflict checking entirely: the local repro deletes an edited new task. Year goals are also classified as task in step(), and latest() has no goals, so their edits are not checked. Rollback writers are unconditional too.
findings.request: Fix with the actual persisted versions after each write and server-conditional update/delete (or an equivalent authoritative conflict guard) covering existing and created tasks/goals/routines and rollback. Do not rely on clock grace or only a pre-read. Add tests for immediate edits, changed newly created records, goal edits and an edit racing between read and write. Until fixed, do not claim whole-set Undo preserves concurrent edits.
findings.additional_path_review: CanvasActivityContext.finishDiff also implements direct-write Undo separately from applyChangeSet: created rows are deleted and c.before fields restored unconditionally, without the later-edit/version guard. Include this direct one-item route in the R1 correction; fixing only card Undo leaves it exposed.

findings.finding: The monetary concurrency claim is incorrect. reserve_ai_provider_call takes a lock but increments only call counts; no money is reserved. Do not test ledger poisoning on production.

findings.finding: Interrupted saves are not proven retry-safe. Local fault injection against actual applyChangeSet committed the first add then lost its response: the function returned reverted:true/kept:[], which the card renders as Nothing was changed. Retrying the exact same two-add card created three fixture rows including a duplicate of the first task. Card creation passes no stable operation/row ID. Separately, direct-create stableRowId includes model-generated title/date spelling; the same user/turn with Call Morgan versus Phone Morgan, or the same instant expressed with -04:00 versus Z, produces different IDs. The endpoint reruns the model on retry rather than replaying an authoritative stored turn result, so same turnId alone is not a complete idempotency guarantee.
findings.request: Add stable persisted operation identities for card Approve and durable replay/deduplication for direct turns, with authorization and exact prior-write preconditions. Distinguish unknown commit outcome from confirmed no-write/rollback; reconcile by operation ID before retry or saying nothing changed. Add regressions for commit followed by lost response, retry/reload of the same card, two devices approving, and model wording/date-format variation on direct retry. Keep hosted interrupted-network proof explicitly pending until exercised on the existing synthetic fixtures. Coordinate with R1 conditional rollback/Undo; do not expand product scope.

findings.finding: Attachment storage authorization can be granted by a caller-controlled metadata row. The INSERT/UPDATE attachment policy checks only user_id=auth.uid(); the storage SELECT policy authorizes any path referenced by a visible attachment. In isolated PostgreSQL, user B could not initially see A's private object or metadata. B then inserted an attachment on B's own task with A's known storage_path. The object became selectable to B, while A's metadata stayed hidden. The private-document restrictive policy does not help because B owns the forged metadata. Existing 35/35 privacy checks exercise only metadata and miss this authorization path. Knowledge of an object path must not confer access.
findings.request: Prioritize before expanding beta. Read the deployed attachment/storage policies without downloading real content, and close the authorization gap with server-enforced ownership/reference validity on insert and update, and a storage policy that cannot derive access solely from attacker-created metadata. Preserve authorized household file sharing. Regressions must cover unrelated household with known path, same-household private document, altered storage_path, legitimate shared attachment, revoked access and signed URL/download behavior on synthetic files. Do not run adversarial access against real family objects; use existing synthetic fixtures or local isolated policy tests.
